Data of a Fitted Model, with the Response on Both Scales

Source: R/pm-data.R
pm_data.Rd

pm_data() returns the rows used to fit a model (after subset and missing values), with the response on the scale of the model and on the original scale: .y is the response as modelled (e.g. log(y + 1); for a GLM the observed response, as a proportion for cbind(successes, failures)), and .y_orig the response on the original scale (y), taken from the data or, when only the transformed response is available, computed with the inverse transformation. A transformation given to predictmeans as trans (for a response transformed before the fit) is used the same way. It is also the generic through which a new model class can say where its data are (see pm_coef).

Usage

pm_data(model, ...)

# Default S3 method
pm_data(model, data = NULL, trans = NULL, ...)

Arguments

model

A fitted model, or a semireg fit.

...

Not used.

data

Optional: the data the model was fitted to, when they cannot be found from the model.

trans

Optional: a function that back-transforms the response (as trans of predictmeans), used when the model formula has an untransformed response.

Value

A data frame with the variables of the data, .y, .y_orig and .weights (prior weights, when there are any), and attribute "response": a list with expr (the response as written, e.g. "log(y + 1)"), name (the response variable, e.g. "y"), scale of the model's means ("identity", "transformed" or "link"), link, family and back (what back-transforms the means: "link", "formula", "trans" or NA).

Examples

  oats <- as.data.frame(nlme::Oats)
  fm <- lm(log(yield + 1) ~ Variety, data = oats)
  d <- pm_data(fm)
  head(d[c("yield", ".y", ".y_orig")])
#>   yield       .y .y_orig
#> 1   111 4.718499     111
#> 2   130 4.875197     130
#> 3   157 5.062595     157
#> 4   174 5.164786     174
#> 5   117 4.770685     117
#> 6   114 4.744932     114
  attr(d, "response")
#> $expr
#> [1] "log(yield + 1)"
#> 
#> $name
#> [1] "yield"
#> 
#> $scale
#> [1] "transformed"
#> 
#> $link
#> NULL
#> 
#> $family
#> [1] "gaussian"
#> 
#> $back
#> [1] "formula"
#>
